newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain govt sees inflation fall in coming months.
newsitem.headline: Spain govt sees inflation fall in coming months.

text.p: Spanish Economy Secretary Cristobal Montoro said on Wednesday that there were signs that inflation should be falling in the coming months.

Montoro predicted that the process of deregulation in government-controlled sectors and commitment not to raise regulated prices above inflation will have "even more positive (effect) in the coming months."
Speaking to a congressional committee, Montoro said there are signs that price growth is being contained, despite a hike in taxes on tobacco and alcohol in July.

"Despite the measures to hike taxes we are confident that price performance this summer will be the best proof that we are currently in a phase of a substantial decline in inflation in Spain," he said.
He also ruled out any new tax increases with inflationary effects in the upcoming budget.
"There will be no more hikes (in taxes) in the 1997 budget which could hurt the CPI," he said.
